query: Most of my money is in cash right now. Is that okay or should I shift it into investments?

recommendations.title: Maintain High Cash Position for Emergency Fund Priority
recommendations.summary: Keep majority of funds in cash to complete your critical emergency fund goal before increasing investment exposure.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: With $15,000 in cash and a $22,000 emergency fund target, you're 68% toward your highest-priority goal. Given your conservative risk tolerance (loss comfort of 3/10), no existing emergency fund, moderate debt ($38,000), and beginner experience, maintaining high cash reserves is the correct strategy. Your monthly expenses are $3,800, so you need $22,800 for a true 6-month cushion. Shifting cash to investments now would expose you to market volatility when you may need these funds within 1-2 years. Once the emergency fund is complete, you can gradually increase equity exposure for your medium-term house down payment goal.
recommendations.suggested_action: Keep current $15,000 cash position and add $7,000-8,000 more to high-yield savings account before increasing investment allocations

recommendations.title: Redirect New Savings to High-Yield Savings Account
recommendations.summary: Channel monthly surplus into HYSA earning 4.5-5.5% to safely complete emergency fund within 12-18 months.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your annual income of $72,000 with $3,800 monthly expenses ($45,600/year) suggests approximately $2,200/month after-tax available. After accounting for debt payments from moderate debt load, you likely have $500-1,000/month surplus. Directing this to a high-yield savings account (currently offering 4.5-5.5% APY) allows you to complete your $22,000 emergency fund within 12-18 months while earning better returns than traditional savings with zero market risk. This aligns perfectly with conservative risk tolerance and your stated priority of building emergency reserves before increasing investment risk.
recommendations.suggested_action: Open high-yield savings account and commit $500-1,000 monthly until emergency fund reaches $22,000-23,000

recommendations.title: Maintain Conservative Investment Mix During Accumulation Phase
recommendations.summary: Your current 40% invested position (30% VTTSX, 10% BND) is appropriately conservative given your profile and goals.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: With $7,500 in VTTSX (target-date fund) and $2,500 in BND (bond fund), your investment allocation is suitable for a beginner with conservative risk tolerance. VTTSX provides diversified, age-appropriate exposure with automatic rebalancing, while BND offers stability. At 28 years old with medium-term horizons, you have some capacity for equity exposure, but your immediate need for emergency funds and moderate existing debt justifies this conservative approach. Once emergency fund is established, you can gradually increase VTTSX contributions for your 5-7 year house down payment goal. Do not liquidate these positions; let them continue growing while you build cash reserves.
recommendations.suggested_action: Maintain current $10,000 investment position; resume contributions only after emergency fund is complete

recommendations.title: Address Debt to Improve Net Worth Position
recommendations.summary: Develop parallel debt reduction strategy alongside emergency fund building to improve your negative net worth.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your current net worth is -$13,000 due to $38,000 in liabilities against $25,000 in assets. While building your emergency fund is the top priority, high-interest debt (credit cards >8%, personal loans) should be addressed concurrently. Consider allocating 70% of monthly surplus to emergency fund and 30% to highest-interest debt elimination. Once emergency fund reaches $15,000-18,000 (4-5 months expenses), you could temporarily shift to 50/50 allocation between final emergency funding and aggressive debt paydown. Lower debt burden will improve cash flow for future investment contributions and reduce financial stress, supporting your conservative risk profile.
recommendations.suggested_action: Identify highest-interest debt and allocate 20-30% of monthly surplus ($150-300) toward accelerated payoff alongside emergency fund contributions
